# libGDX Headless Polygon Geometry CLI

## Background
You are building a deterministic command-line geometry utility on top of libGDX's headless backend. The tool reads a small text-based scripting language describing 2D convex polygons and queries, then evaluates each query using libGDX math primitives (notably `com.badlogic.gdx.math.Intersector` and `com.badlogic.gdx.math.Polygon`) inside a `HeadlessApplication` and writes one result per query to standard output. No OpenGL context, no native windowing, and no audio must be initialized.

## Requirements
- Implement a Gradle-based libGDX project at `/home/user/myproject` that runs entirely with the headless backend (`com.badlogicgames.gdx:gdx-backend-headless:1.14.2`).
- Pin the libGDX version to `1.14.2` (core `com.badlogicgames.gdx:gdx:1.14.2`).
- Wire an `ApplicationListener` (or `ApplicationAdapter`) that runs under `new HeadlessApplication(listener, config)` with `config.updatesPerSecond = 0` so the program ticks once and exits.
- Read the path to the script file from the first program argument (forwarded via `--args`).
- For each non-empty, non-comment line in the script, execute exactly one of the commands below and print exactly one output line to stdout. Use libGDX's `Intersector` and `Polygon` classes for the geometric primitives.
- After processing every line, call `Gdx.app.exit()` and join the main loop thread cleanly.
- A `run.sh` wrapper script must be provided at the project root that accepts the script-file path as the first argument and forwards it to the headless launcher, writing only the program's stdout lines (no Gradle banner / progress output) to stdout.
- A line starting with `#` or a blank line is ignored.

### Script language
All coordinates are floating point numbers. Polygon names match `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*`. Polygons defined by the script are convex and given in counter-clockwise order.

- `POLY <name> <x1> <y1> <x2> <y2> ... <xn> <yn>` — store a polygon with the given vertex coordinates (at least 3 vertices, so at least 6 numbers).
  - Output: `POLY <name> <vertexCount>`
- `OVERLAP <a> <b>` — test whether convex polygons `<a>` and `<b>` overlap using `Intersector.overlapConvexPolygons`.
  - Output: `OVERLAP <a> <b> true` or `OVERLAP <a> <b> false`
- `CONTAINS <name> <x> <y>` — test whether point `(x, y)` is inside polygon `<name>` using `Intersector.isPointInPolygon` on the stored vertex array.
  - Output: `CONTAINS <name> <x> <y> true` or `CONTAINS <name> <x> <y> false`
  - Print the input coordinates back exactly as they appeared in the script line (preserve the formatting tokens the user typed).
- `SEGMENTS <ax> <ay> <bx> <by> <cx> <cy> <dx> <dy>` — intersect segment `AB` with segment `CD` using `Intersector.intersectSegments(Vector2, Vector2, Vector2, Vector2, Vector2)`.
  - If the segments meet, output: `SEGMENTS hit <px> <py>` where `<px>` and `<py>` are the intersection point coordinates rounded to **three decimal places** using `Locale.ROOT` (use `String.format(Locale.ROOT, "%.3f", value)`).
  - Otherwise, output: `SEGMENTS miss`
- `AREA <name>` — compute the signed area of polygon `<name>` via `Polygon.area()`.
  - Output: `AREA <name> <value>` where `<value>` is rounded to three decimal places using `Locale.ROOT`.

An unknown command, a reference to an undefined polygon, or a malformed numeric token must cause the program to print `ERROR <line-number> <command-or-reason>` (1-based line number counting blank and comment lines) and continue to the next line.

## Implementation Hints
- The `gdx-backend-headless` artifact pulls in the desktop natives loader, so a plain Gradle `application` plugin run is sufficient — no LWJGL window is required.
- `Intersector.overlapConvexPolygons` accepts `com.badlogic.gdx.math.Polygon` instances. `Intersector.isPointInPolygon` takes a `float[]` (or `(float[] polygon, int offset, int count, float x, float y)`).
- `HeadlessApplicationConfiguration.updatesPerSecond = 0` runs the loop as fast as possible; you can do all your work in `create()` and then call `Gdx.app.exit()`.
- Read the script through `Gdx.files.absolute(path)` or plain `java.nio.file.Files` — both work under the headless `Files` implementation.
- Make sure your `run.sh` filters out Gradle's own logging (e.g. use `./gradlew -q` or capture only the launcher's stdout) so that the only lines emitted are the result lines defined above.
- The headless launcher runs the `ApplicationListener` on its own thread; wait for the main loop to finish before exiting `main()` so all output is flushed.

package com.example;

import com.badlogic.gdx.ApplicationAdapter;
import com.badlogic.gdx.Gdx;
import com.badlogic.gdx.backends.headless.HeadlessApplication;
import com.badlogic.gdx.backends.headless.HeadlessApplicationConfiguration;
import com.badlogic.gdx.math.Intersector;
import com.badlogic.gdx.math.Polygon;
import com.badlogic.gdx.math.Vector2;

import java.io.BufferedReader;
import java.io.FileReader;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Paths;
import java.util.HashMap;
import java.util.Locale;
import java.util.Map;

public class PolygonGeometryApp extends ApplicationAdapter {
    private static String scriptPath;
    
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        if (args.length < 1) {
            System.err.println("Usage: <script-file>");
            System.exit(1);
        }
        scriptPath = args[0];
        
        HeadlessApplicationConfiguration config = new HeadlessApplicationConfiguration();
        config.updatesPerSecond = 0;
        new HeadlessApplication(new PolygonGeometryApp(), config);
    }
    
    @Override
    public void create() {
        try {
            processScript(scriptPath);
        } catch (Exception e) {
            e.printStackTrace();
        } finally {
            Gdx.app.exit();
        }
    }
    
    private void processScript(String path) throws Exception {
        Map<String, Polygon> polygons = new HashMap<>();
        Map<String, float[]> vertices = new HashMap<>();
        
        try (BufferedReader reader = Files.newBufferedReader(Paths.get(path))) {
            String line;
            int lineNumber = 0;
            while ((line = reader.readLine()) != null) {
                lineNumber++;
                String trimmed = line.trim();
                if (trimmed.isEmpty() || trimmed.startsWith("#")) {
                    continue;
                }
                processLine(trimmed, lineNumber, polygons, vertices, line);
            }
        }
    }
    
    private void processLine(String line, int lineNumber, Map<String, Polygon> polygons, Map<String, float[]> vertices, String originalLine) {
        String[] tokens = line.split("\\s+");
        String cmd = tokens[0];
        
        try {
            switch (cmd) {
                case "POLY": {
                    if (tokens.length < 2 + 6) {
                        System.out.println("ERROR " + lineNumber + " POLY");
                        return;
                    }
                    String name = tokens[1];
                    int count = (tokens.length - 2);
                    if (count % 2 != 0 || count < 6) {
                        System.out.println("ERROR " + lineNumber + " POLY");
                        return;
                    }
                    float[] verts = new float[count];
                    try {
                        for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
                            verts[i] = Float.parseFloat(tokens[2 + i]);
                        }
                    } catch (NumberFormatException e) {
                        System.out.println("ERROR " + lineNumber + " POLY");
                        return;
                    }
                    polygons.put(name, new Polygon(verts));
                    vertices.put(name, verts);
                    int vertexCount = count / 2;
                    System.out.println("POLY " + name + " " + vertexCount);
                    break;
                }
                case "OVERLAP": {
                    if (tokens.length != 3) {
                        System.out.println("ERROR " + lineNumber + " OVERLAP");
                        return;
                    }
                    String a = tokens[1];
                    String b = tokens[2];
                    Polygon pa = polygons.get(a);
                    Polygon pb = polygons.get(b);
                    if (pa == null || pb == null) {
                        System.out.println("ERROR " + lineNumber + " OVERLAP");
                        return;
                    }
                    boolean result = Intersector.overlapConvexPolygons(pa, pb);
                    System.out.println("OVERLAP " + a + " " + b + " " + result);
                    break;
                }
                case "CONTAINS": {
                    if (tokens.length != 4) {
                        System.out.println("ERROR " + lineNumber + " CONTAINS");
                        return;
                    }
                    String name = tokens[1];
                    String xStr = tokens[2];
                    String yStr = tokens[3];
                    float[] verts = vertices.get(name);
                    if (verts == null) {
                        System.out.println("ERROR " + lineNumber + " CONTAINS");
                        return;
                    }
                    float x, y;
                    try {
                        x = Float.parseFloat(xStr);
                        y = Float.parseFloat(yStr);
                    } catch (NumberFormatException e) {
                        System.out.println("ERROR " + lineNumber + " CONTAINS");
                        return;
                    }
                    boolean result = Intersector.isPointInPolygon(verts, x, y);
                    System.out.println("CONTAINS " + name + " " + xStr + " " + yStr + " " + result);
                    break;
                }
                case "SEGMENTS": {
                    if (tokens.length != 9) {
                        System.out.println("ERROR " + lineNumber + " SEGMENTS");
                        return;
                    }
                    float ax, ay, bx, by, cx, cy, dx, dy;
                    try {
                        ax = Float.parseFloat(tokens[1]);
                        ay = Float.parseFloat(tokens[2]);
                        bx = Float.parseFloat(tokens[3]);
                        by = Float.parseFloat(tokens[4]);
                        cx = Float.parseFloat(tokens[5]);
                        cy = Float.parseFloat(tokens[6]);
                        dx = Float.parseFloat(tokens[7]);
                        dy = Float.parseFloat(tokens[8]);
                    } catch (NumberFormatException e) {
                        System.out.println("ERROR " + lineNumber + " SEGMENTS");
                        return;
                    }
                    Vector2 p1 = new Vector2(ax, ay);
                    Vector2 p2 = new Vector2(bx, by);
                    Vector2 p3 = new Vector2(cx, cy);
                    Vector2 p4 = new Vector2(dx, dy);
                    Vector2 intersection = new Vector2();
                    if (Intersector.intersectSegments(p1, p2, p3, p4, intersection)) {
                        System.out.println("SEGMENTS hit " + 
                            String.format(Locale.ROOT, "%.3f", intersection.x) + " " + 
                            String.format(Locale.ROOT, "%.3f", intersection.y));
                    } else {
                        System.out.println("SEGMENTS miss");
                    }
                    break;
                }
                case "AREA": {
                    if (tokens.length != 2) {
                        System.out.println("ERROR " + lineNumber + " AREA");
                        return;
                    }
                    String name = tokens[1];
                    Polygon p = polygons.get(name);
                    if (p == null) {
                        System.out.println("ERROR " + lineNumber + " AREA");
                        return;
                    }
                    float area = p.area();
                    System.out.println("AREA " + name + " " + String.format(Locale.ROOT, "%.3f", area));
                    break;
                }
                default:
                    System.out.println("ERROR " + lineNumber + " " + cmd);
            }
        } catch (Exception e) {
            System.out.println("ERROR " + lineNumber + " " + cmd);
        }
    }
}

# Wrapper that forwards the script path to the libGDX headless launcher and
# emits only the program's stdout lines (no Gradle banner / progress noise).
set -e

if [ "$#" -lt 1 ]; then
    echo "Usage: $0 <script-file>" >&2
    exit 1
fi

SCRIPT_FILE="$1"

# Resolve project root from this script's directory so it works regardless of
# the caller's current working directory.
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
cd "$SCRIPT_DIR"

# -q suppresses Gradle's INFO-level logging. We still capture stdout/stderr so
# any unexpected Gradle output is hidden, leaving only the launcher's result
# lines visible to the caller.
exec ./gradlew -q --console=plain run --args "$SCRIPT_FILE"

# Wrapper that forwards the script path to the libGDX headless launcher and
